title: Serving runtime weekly update — kernel / KV cache / batching (2026-08-26)
content:
Summary:
This week we focused on three coordinated efforts: kernel optimizations for fused attention and matmul paths, incremental improvements to the KV cache (eviction and lock contention), and an A/B experiment on batching policies. We hit good perf wins on end-to-end latency for short-chat requests but observed regressions under high-concurrency tails that we need to mitigate next week.

Standup highlights (8/24–8/26):
- Marco: landed fused-attention microkernel prototype on x86 (PR #821). Observed ~18% token throughput improvement on synthetic 1–8 seq workloads. Notable: single-thread scalar fallback still slower for seq>4 — investigating vectorized fallback path.
- Leah: KV cache refactor (SRV-912) branch updated. Reduced global lock hold time by moving hot-path metrics to thread-local counters; raw lock contention decreased ~60% in bench harness. However, memory churn increased under heavy eviction.
- Omar: Batching experiment rollout (SRV-918) — started canary traffic (10% of hosted API) with adaptive windowing + priority queue. Average latency improved 12% for batched model routes, but 95th increased by 8% for small requests due to delayed micro-batches.
- Sofia: telemetry and tracing: added per-request KV-hit/miss tag and microkernel usage flag to traces. This helped pinpoint requests hitting scalar fallback and high miss-rate clients.

Perf and metrics:
- Fused attention microkernel (local bench): +18% tokens/sec on 1–8 seq, +6% on 16–32 seq. Single-thread latency P50 down 9%.
- End-to-end on canary (latest runtime + kernel): P50 160ms -> 142ms; P95 410ms -> 438ms (regression).
- KV cache contention: lock hold time reduced from 3.4ms -> 1.3ms median in harness; production traces show similar trend but memory allocations per second increased ~22% on canary nodes.
- Batching experiment: throughput up 9% overall on batched routes, small-request tail regressions concentrated on routes with median tokens < 20.

Root causes identified:
1) Scalar fallback in fused-attn kernel triggered by specific sequence alignment and small batch sizes — this path is not yet vectorized.
2) KV cache eviction currently uses a coarse-grained global LRU list; refactor to sharded LRU helped lock contention but increased per-shard memory churn and duplicate metadata. Need a better bounded eviction structure.
3) Adaptive batching window waits for a small timeout to form micro-batches; for routes with strict P95 SLOs and very low token counts this timeout adds harmful latency.

Decisions made:
- Roll forward fused-attn kernel to wider internal canary (50% of runtime nodes) while we ship vectorized fallback in next patch. Rationale: majority of traffic benefits and scalar fallback path is rare but needs fix before public release. (Owner: Marco)
- Revert adaptive window for routes tagged "latency-sensitive"; keep it enabled for cost-sensitive batched routes. Add route-level opt-out flag in config. (Owner: Omar)
- For KV cache, stop-gap: revert to previously stable eviction threshold for canary to reduce memory churn; long-term: design bounded sharded LRU with per-shard allocation caps (Leah + infra).

Action items / next week priorities:
- Marco: implement SSE/AVX vectorized fallback for fused-attn scalar path; test correctness across fp16/quantized int8 kernels. Blockers: two failing edge cases on long-prefix masks. Target: PR by 2026-09-02.
- Leah: prototype bounded-sharded-LRU design doc and simulation (memory vs hit-rate tradeoffs). Add metrics to simulate duplicate metadata cost. Target: doc + bench by 2026-09-02.
- Omar: update batching rollout to respect route-level latency flag; add dynamic timeout tuning based on per-route P95. Expand canary to 25% after revert. Target: config + rollout plan by 2026-08-30.
- Sofia: add alert rule for production KV allocation rate spike and trace sampler focused on scalar-fallback occurrences. Target: alert + dashboard tile by 2026-08-28.
- QA/Bench: run 72-hour soak with new kernel on isolated cluster and capture allocation/GC statistics.

Open questions / risks:
- Memory cost impact: bounded shards may lower global contention but could harm hit-rate for some workloads (esp. long-conversation chat). Need offline trace simulations.
- Long-tail latency: if vectorized fallback doesn't cover all edge cases, we might need a hybrid runtime policy to prefer older kernel for latency-sensitive routes.
- Release timing: engineering wants to ship fused-attn to decrease unit compute costs; SRE is concerned about P95 regressions during peak. Need cross-team sync before public rollout.

Meeting notes (syncs this week):
- Tue 2026-08-25 10:00 — kernel sync (attendance: Marco, Aisha, Leah, Ryan infra): reviewed microkernel perf, agreed on vector fallback priority. Action: Marco to add correctness harness for mask-edge cases.
- Wed 2026-08-26 15:00 — batching retro (attendance: Omar, Leah, product-hosted-api rep): reviewed canary metrics. Product asked for route flag and quick rollback plan.
- Thu 2026-08-26 09:30 — cross-team triage (attendance: SRE lead, Product ops): discussed target SLOs and stepwise rollout strategy; agreed to hold public rollout until vectorization PR passes canary soak.

Notes to self / informal TODOs:
- Re-check PR #821 microkernel for unexplained NaN in int8 perf run (seen once in CI).
- Add a small local script to replay traces that hit scalar-fallback for easier debugging.
- Align with infra on node memory overcommit thresholds before next canary expansion.

Related PRs and references:
- PR #821: fused-attention microkernel prototype (Marco)
- PR #834: KV cache sharding and thread-local counters (Leah)
- SRV-912: KV cache eviction redesign
- SRV-918: Adaptive batching rollout

Overall: solid progress on the high-impact kernel work; wins are visible in median latency and throughput. Main work next week is eliminating scalar-fallback regressions and stabilizing KV memory behavior so we can expand the canary without increasing production tail latency.

-- Aisha
